review: Independent B02 G3 contract v2 review for test-oracle readiness
scope: Read-only review of the revised supplemental G3 contract against the approved B02 identity plan and pinned local Authlib source/API. No product code or tests were written or executed.

reviewed_contract_points.assessment: The revised contract now agrees with the approved parent plan: the HMAC-SHA256 result is unpadded Base64URL and exactly 43 URL-safe characters. The input is csrf_key || ASCII("ifpmic.csrf.v1") || one actual NUL byte || ASCII(ax_session). The byte-level derivation is sufficiently fixed for an independent literal HMAC oracle.

Authorization, token, and JWKS endpoints may use distinct explicitly configured HTTPS origins, while each network operation is restricted to its exact configured method and full URL. Discovery and token-selected URLs remain prohibited. Issuer remains an exact ID-token claim value and is no longer incorrectly coupled to endpoint origin. This makes a realistic split-origin synthetic provider testable without broadening the egress policy.

The literal contract is clear: exp > injected now, nbf <= now, iat <= now, with leeway zero; each NumericDate is finite numeric and not boolean. Authlib 1.9.1 exposes CodeIDToken.validate(self, now=None, leeway=0), but its pinned JWT claims validator rejects exp only when exp < now, so equality is accepted by that validator. The implementation must apply the stricter contract exp > now check explicitly; the independent TC oracle must assert that exp == now is rejected. This is a known implementation hazard, not an ambiguity in the expected result.

The contract specifies a string aud or a nonempty unique list of strings containing client_id. Multi-audience values require azp == client_id; if azp is present for a single audience it must also match. The pinned Authlib CodeIDToken validates configured aud options and azp consistency, but the application must still enforce the contract's unique-list/type rules. Literal TC cases can distinguish single vs multiple audience, absent/mismatched azp, duplicate aud, wrong client, and wrong claim types.

The configured algorithm set, exact issuer, matching nonce, required claims, bounded public asymmetric JWKS, fixed JWKS endpoint, optional response iss check, and at_hash verification inputs are stated explicitly. A local signed provider can independently vary each claim and signature while retaining a valid baseline. No real IdP is needed for G3 contract tests.

Routes, query allowlist/limits, browser-bound one-time state, consume-before-exchange behavior, cross-browser mismatch semantics, cookie attributes, session/idle boundary, stable CSRF across restart, logout status mapping, duplicate-header handling, exact CORS policy, fixed errors, and actual Uvicorn log-canary requirement provide independent normal, exception, boundary, race, and regression oracles.

required_test_case_groups: Valid authorization-code/PKCE callback with exact token endpoint and a JWKS endpoint on a separately configured HTTPS origin; verify issuer remains exact and no discovery occurs.

ID-token claims and crypto matrix including exp just-before/equal/after now, nbf and iat equal boundaries, booleans/nonfinite values, aud scalar/list/duplicate/wrong client, multi-aud azp, nonce, issuer, signature, algorithm, key, and at_hash.

Browser-state isolation, duplicate callback parameters, malformed encoding, callback size caps, provider errors, redirect/non-2xx/invalid_grant, nonidentity content encoding, streamed response limit, timeout, proxy-environment isolation, and fresh-login requirement after consumed-state failure.

Session cookie rotation/hash-only persistence, exact expiry and idle boundaries, restart-stable literal CSRF, CSRF/Origin duplicates and failures, logout/revocation, and before/after-commit fault behavior.

Actual loopback Uvicorn callback canary checks across successful, failed, expired, and replayed callbacks; assert absence of code/state/error_description in stdout, stderr, and captured app logs without echoing canaries in test failures.

resolved_by: Explicit unpadded Base64URL with exact 43-character CSRF output.
Exact configured method/full-URL allowlist across separately configured HTTPS endpoint origins.

limitations: Contract review only; no implementation or TC candidate has been reviewed or accepted.
No real identity provider, corporate SSO, proxy, or production endpoint was contacted.
Local synthetic-provider success does not complete original AT-21 or prove reverse-proxy log redaction.
